standard_prerequisites.name: A projective module over a local ring is free, and Lazard's theorem on flat modules as filtered colimits of finite free modules
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, labels algebra-theorem-projective-free-over-local-ring (proof line 1955) and algebra-theorem-lazard (proof line 1960)
standard_prerequisites.use: The first reduces to the case of a finite free source, and the second writes the target as a directed colimit of finite free modules.

standard_prerequisites.name: Splitting of an injection of finite free modules over a local ring detected modulo the maximal ideal
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, elementary fact used at proof lines 1967-1968
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that the reduction of the map being injective implies that the map into each sufficiently late finite free piece is a split injection, which is what makes it stay injective after tensoring with any module.

core_obligations: Reduce to a finite free source: since a projective module over a local ring is free and the statement for finitely generated direct summands implies the general one, one may assume the source is finite free (proof lines 1953-1958).

Write the target as a colimit and factor the map: express the flat target as a directed colimit of finite free modules, and since the source is finitely generated the map factors through one of them (proof lines 1958-1962).

Conclude universal injectivity: the injectivity of the reduction persists to all later stages, so the map into every sufficiently late finite free piece is a split injection, hence remains injective after tensoring with any module, and tensoring commutes with the colimit, giving universal injectivity (proof lines 1963-1972).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to a finite free source (proof lines 1953-1958).
Colimit presentation and factorisation of the map (proof lines 1958-1962).
Split injection after tensoring and colimit compatibility (proof lines 1963-1972).
difficulty_reason: The lemma gives a local criterion for universal injectivity: for a map from a projective module to a flat module over a local ring whose reduction modulo the maximal ideal is injective, the map is universally injective (statement lines 1945-1951, tag 05FX-adjacent). The proof reduces to a finite free source, writes the flat target as a directed colimit of finite free modules and factors the map through one of them, observes that injectivity of the reduction persists so that the map into each late piece is a split injection, and concludes by compatibility of tensoring with colimits. The splitting step is the substance, so the claim is H2.
